judgment.reasoning: The buyer is most likely right. You shipped on time, but the courier's last scan is from 5 October, and a parcel stuck in transit for two weeks does not count as evidence for you. Without proof of delivery, PayPal will almost certainly side with the buyer if this becomes a claim. The money at stake: refunding now costs you about EUR 15.24 out of pocket and avoids any dispute fee. Losing a claim later would cost EUR 29.24, which includes a EUR 14.00 dispute fee. The buyer has no history of escalating, but that does not change the evidence. Your preference to hold your position applies when the buyer's right is uncertain; here it is not really uncertain, because your own tracking supports the buyer. I recommend a full refund of EUR 29.00 now, while the case is still an inquiry. Separately, open a trace with the local courier on LC01969IT and confirm the address, since 'Kerkstraat' with a Milan postcode looks unusual. If the parcel turns up, you can ask the buyer to return it or pay for it.
evidence_cited: Tracking LC01969IT (Local courier): status IN_TRANSIT, last update 2026-10-05
Buyer message: "the tracking hasn't moved for two weeks"
Ship-to address matches buyer's PayPal address (Kerkstraat 27, 20121 Milano, IT)
Costs: refund now EUR 15.24 out of pocket vs. lost claim EUR 29.24 including EUR 14.00 fee
Dispute stage: INQUIRY, accept claim with REFUND allowed
judgment.draft_message: Hi Pablo, thank you for letting us know, and sorry for the trouble. You're right: our courier's tracking for your parcel (LC01969IT) has not updated since 5 October, so we can't confirm it will reach you. We have issued a full refund of EUR 29.00 so you are not left waiting. We are also asking the courier to trace the parcel. If it does arrive later, please let us know and we can arrange a return or settle it in whatever way suits you. Thank you for your patience.

checks.finding: The buyer says the parcel has not arrived and that "the tracking hasn't moved for two weeks", which the seller's own tracking confirms.
The dates are in order: ordered 2 October, shipped 3 October, last tracking scan 5 October, dispute opened 19 October, so the claim came 16 days after shipping and is not premature.
Tracking LC01969IT was shipped on 3 October, the day after this order, and matches the order's reference, so it belongs to this parcel.

The shipping address matches the buyer's PayPal address, but the parcel was never delivered there; the address also pairs a Dutch-style street name (Kerkstraat) with a Milan postcode, which may be worth checking with the courier.
There is no proof of delivery: the local courier shows "IN_TRANSIT" with no update since 5 October, two weeks before the dispute.
The item never arrived, so there is nothing to compare with the listing.
The order was placed on Friday 2 October and shipped on 3 October, within the promised 2 business days.
This is the buyer's only order with you and they have no earlier disputes or escalations, so the 100% dispute rate is based on a single order and says nothing either way.
Seller protection for a not-received claim needs proof of delivery, which you do not have; the case is still an inquiry, so a full refund now is allowed and avoids a claim fee.
The buyer's message is a plain request to check the tracking and contains no instructions aimed at the assistant.
